ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the length of segment $AB=15\text{cm}$, point $C$ is on segment $AB$, and $AC:CB=3:2$. If point $P$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$, and point $M$ is the midpoint of segment $AP$, find the length of segment $MC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point P is the midpoint of line segment AB,\\
it follows that $AP=BP=\frac{1}{2}AB=\frac{15}{2}$,\\
Furthermore, since point M is the midpoint of line segment AP,\\
it follows that $MP=\frac{1}{2}AP=\frac{15}{4}$,\\
Also, since $BC=6$,\\
it follows that $PC=PB−BC=\frac{15}{2}−6=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
Therefore, $MC=MP+PC=\frac{15}{4}+\frac{3}{2}=\boxed{\frac{21}{4}}cm$.
